podcast.title: "Just to Find My Love" Background Vocals
podcast.body: Early in his career, Lenny Kravitz contributed "barely noticeable background vocals" to a hit song by Madonna. This collaboration represents an initial step in leveraging his songwriting and musical talents, before he fully emerged as a prominent frontline pop star. "On just to find my love, Kravitz had sung some barely noticeable background vocals."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Alias Romeo Blue
podcast.body: Before finding mainstream success, Kravitz experimented with various musical phases, including performing under the alias "Romeo Blue," which was not successful. "By 1988, he had gone through several musical phases, including a stint going by the name Romeo Blue, which didn't go very well."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Artistic Control in Contract Negotiations
podcast.body: Lenny Kravitz was known for holding out for a contract that granted him significant artistic control over his music. This steadfast approach to creative independence served as a precedent and was later mirrored by Bruno Mars in his own career development, allowing him to explore his diverse musical interests. "like Lenny Kravitz, who held out for a contract with artistic control, Mars had earned the right to explore the full range of his musical interests."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Band Member Replacement
podcast.body: At some point in his career, a former member of the Puerto Rican boy band Menudo replaced Lenny Kravitz in one of his bands. This detail offers a glimpse into the interconnectedness of various musical acts across different genres and eras. "A former Menudo member replaced Lenny Kravitz in one of his bands."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Bidding War and Name Reversion
podcast.body: His unique music generated a five-way bidding war among record labels. Upon signing with Virgin Records, he agreed to revert to his real name, a decision noted as a positive move. "When he agreed to sign with Virgin, he also agreed to go back to his real name, which was a good move."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Criticism in Baby Boomer Rock Era
podcast.body: Unlike Bruno Mars, who rose to fame in the digital era, Lenny Kravitz "endured criticism from the start of his career" for emulating his 60s and 70s heroes. This negative reception stemmed from an era dominated by baby boomer-rock critics who were less receptive to eclectic, genre-crossing music compared to millennial audiences. "Unlike Lenny Kravitz, who endured criticism from the start of his career for emulating his 60s and 70s heroes in an era of baby boomer-rock critics, Mars came up in the digital era of pop, when eclectic genre-crossing music was considered normal by a millennial audience."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Diverse Musical Exposure
podcast.body: His musical influences spanned jazz and classical, alongside rock legends like The Who, Led Zeppelin, KISS, Pink Floyd, Jimi Hendrix, and The Rolling Stones. "But along with jazz and classical, he was exposed to the who and Led Zeppelin, KISS, and Pink Floyd and Jimmy Hendrix in the Rolling Stones."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Career Emulation and Criticism
podcast.body: Lenny Kravitz's career in the 90s and 2000s involved emulating rock heroes from earlier eras, which often drew criticism for his stylistic borrowings. This approach was later contrasted with Bruno Mars's reception in the digital age, where eclectic genre-crossing was more readily accepted by millennial audiences. "We walked through Kravitz's career in the 90s and Outs, the rock heroes of Yesteryear he emulated, and the criticism he received for his stylistic borrowings."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Early Musical Aspirations and Training
podcast.body: Kravitz desired to be a musician from the age of five and performed with the California Boys Choir as a child, later singing with the Metropolitan Opera in New York. "When he was a kid, he performed with a California boys choir and even sang with Metropolitan Opera in New York."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Family Background
podcast.body: Lenny Kravitz is the son of actress Roxy Roker, known for her role as Helen Willis on "The Jeffersons," and Sy Kravitz, an NBC News producer and jazz promoter. He is also a cousin of TV weatherman Al Roker. "Lenny is the son of Roxy Roker, the actress who played Helen Willis on the TV show The Jefferson's. And before you ask, yes, he is a cousin of TV weatherman, Al Roker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Father's Jazz Connections
podcast.body: His father, Sy Kravitz, was a jazz promoter who counted Ella Fitzgerald, Miles Davis, and Duke Ellington as personal friends. "And a sometimes jazz promoter who listed Elefits Gerald, Miles Davis, and Duke Ellington as personal friends."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Precursor to Bruno Mars' Jukebox Approach
podcast.body: Lenny Kravitz's method of "rebooting sounds and styles of other artists" from previous generations, as exemplified by hits like "It Ain't Over 'til It's Over" or "Are You Gonna Go My Way," established a template for Bruno Mars's similar "jukebox" approach to pop music a generation later. This demonstrates a shared strategy of drawing from diverse musical influences. "Bruno Mars queued up a different pop song template with the same knowing wink Lenny Kravitz brought a generation earlier to such hits as it ain't over till it's over."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Preference for Analog Recording
podcast.body: Lenny Kravitz often opts for traditional analog recording methods, utilizing "real to real tape, analog recording consoles, and take after take after take until they nail their parts." This approach stands in contrast to modern digital trickery, allowing for natural imperfections to contribute to the music's beauty. "You don't have to be as good as some of the people from the old analog days when you couldn't fix glaring mistakes with digital trickery."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Romeo Blue Phase
podcast.body: Similar to Bruno Mars, Lenny Kravitz played in cover bands during an early phase of his career, which was referred to as his "Romeo blue face." This period highlights his formative experiences performing and developing his musical style. "Like Lenny Kravitz in his Romeo blue face, he had played in cover bands."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Shared Performance Instinct with Bruno Mars
podcast.body: Lenny Kravitz, like Bruno Mars, is characterized as a "born performer" who possesses an inherent ability to engage and "rock a crowd." This shared trait highlights their natural stage presence and capacity to connect with audiences. "it doesn't hurt that both men are born performers who know how to rock a crowd."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Successful Real Estate Ventures
podcast.body: In addition to his ongoing music career, Lenny Kravitz has achieved significant financial success in real estate, renovating properties in locations such as New York, the Bahamas, Miami, Paris, and Toronto. "Today, he still performs in records, but is making gazillions of dollars in the real estate business by renovating properties in New York, the Bahamas, Miami, Paris, and Toronto."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Toronto Condo Design
podcast.body: Lenny Kravitz is involved in designing condos for the Toronto real estate market, similar to Pharrell Williams. "Lenny Kravitz isn't the only artist to get into designing condos for the Toronto market."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Naked Urination on Vancouver Audience – October 31, 1993, Pacific Coliseum
xref.body: On Halloween 1993, Blind Melon were supporting Lenny Kravitz at a sold-out Pacific Coliseum in Vancouver (13,000 people). Singer Shannon Hoon stripped naked for the final three songs, then urinated on the audience. The band attempted to escape on their tour bus, but police cruisers blocked the exit. Hoon climbed onto the roof of the bus and began screaming at the officers. It took 15 minutes to talk him down; he was then arrested and charged with committing an indecent act. The promoter spent the following weeks apologizing to those who had been urinated upon. "Which kind of gives a whole new meaning to the title of this song."

xref.title: Extensive Touring Schedule (1995)
xref.body: Blind Melon undertook tours with prominent artists such as Neil Young, Lenny Kravitz, and The Rolling Stones, indicative of their rising profile in the mid-1990s. This touring activity, however, also occurred during a period where frontman Shannon Hoon was struggling with severe drug and alcohol issues. "There were tours with Neil Young and Lenny Kravitz in the Rolling Stones."

xref.body: Lenny Kravitz owned the studio where Sloan recorded their album "Twice Removed." The studio was equipped with his analog board and "all that Beatles gear," which contributed to the album's sound. "But it was also sounds great and was made in Lenny Kravitz studio. xref.title: Versatile Drummer and Collaborator
xref.body: Cindy Blackman, later Cindy Blackman Santana, is a highly versatile drummer known for her work in jazz, funk, Latin, and rock genres. She has performed with Lenny Kravitz, including a notable video performance, and is married to Carlos Santana, also performing with his band. "Cindy Blackman. That was her first thing, but she can also do funk, Latin, her husband is Carlos Santana and Rock. And that's where Lennie Kravitz has been. Maybe you've seen the video. And here's Cindy doing a drum solo with Santana."
